narrative.pretitle: Synaiq KIP｜A platform for business decisions and reasoning
title: Behind the numbers,
a business story unfolds.
paragraphs: From investigating causes to comparing outcomes, put accumulated enterprise knowledge to work in your next business decision.
KIP connects documents, reports and experience, retrieves relevant evidence, reasons through possible causes and calculates outcomes from data and assumptions to help teams compare their options.

KIP has no token-based fees, and sensitive data need not be sent to external online models. Use retrieval, reasoning and computation to support business decisions while retaining control of company data.

title: AI is changing
how companies allocate budgets.
outlook.intro: According to Investing.com’s account of a J.P. Morgan survey, the CIOs surveyed expected AI-accelerated computing hardware to take a larger share of IT budgets.
reading: In the 2024 survey, 33% of CIOs said they were cutting funding for other IT projects to support AI investment. Legacy systems, upgrades and infrastructure were most affected.
Yet 62% said they were not cutting other projects. The report suggested that most AI investment would be funded by additional budgets, rather than simply reallocating existing spending.
outlook.chartLabel: AI computing hardware's share of IT budgets: 5% in 2024 to an expected 14.5% in 2027, implying approximately 42.6% compound annual growth in the share, not actual spending growth
outlook.growthLabel: AI hardware budget share · Implied annual growth
outlook.spending: Together, the respondents oversaw $123 billion in annual enterprise IT spending.
outlook.caveat: These were respondents’ expectations in 2024—not realized results or evidence of Synaiq KIP’s performance.
outlook.detailsLabel: Read the survey context and source
outlook.details: We calculate the implied compound annual growth rate from the reported endpoints: (14.5 ÷ 5)^(1 ÷ 3) − 1 ≈ 42.6%. This measures expected growth in AI hardware's budget share, not growth in total IT budgets or actual spending. It does not imply the same rate in every year. The article describes the rate as roughly 45%, which differs slightly from the calculation using the published endpoints.
outlook.sourceCaveat: Based on media reporting; the full original J.P. Morgan survey was not available for review.
